long_form.title_primary: You Have 60 Seconds Before the Doors Won't Open
title_challengers: What Happens To You When Your Car Sinks
Your Car Just Went Into the Water. Here's Every Second.
long_form.description:
Your car goes into the water and the clock starts — you have about sixty seconds before the doors physically will not open. Here's every second of it.

This is a real-time, second-by-second walkthrough of what the water does to the car and to your body: the float phase that feels like safety, the invisible force that seals the doors, the one exit that's still open, and the quiet at the end that fools people. Not a compilation, not a tips list — a simulation you're inside.

Animation in this video is AI-generated. Scenario researched from vehicle-submersion survival studies.

Sources (verify before publish): vehicle-submersion egress research on float-window duration, door pressure-differential forces, the ~60s electrical window, and tempered vs. laminated glass. Framing is simulation and suggestion only — no operational detail beyond public water-safety guidance.

primary.concept: Submerged-cabin POV: water rising to chest height, the car interior dark except one hazard-orange dashboard clock glowing as the single anomaly. Deep indigo field, >=50% negative space (black water). No face, no gore. Delivers the countdown promise without restating the title.

challengers.concept: Exterior stylized shot: a lone car silhouette tipping into black water, headlights still glowing beneath the surface as the anomaly, hazard-orange accent on the water line. Tests the counterintuitive float-phase angle (pairs with the 'When Your Car Sinks' title).

POV of a single hand on a half-open side window underwater, water pouring over the glass edge lit hazard-orange, deep indigo surround, heavy negative space. Tests the escape-route angle (pairs with the 'Here's Every Second' title).

long_form.pinned_comment: Everyone assumes they'd stay calm. Be honest — in that first 30 seconds while the car is still floating and the dash is still lit, what do you think you'd actually do?
